title: ASSIGNMENT – 2b
subtitle: Multi-Client Student Record Retrieval Using TCP and UDP Sockets
name: Srikrishna O S

sections.heading: AIM
paragraph: To develop a client-server application in Python that lets students retrieve their academic information from a university server. The server reads student records from a CSV file (students.csv) containing Roll Number, Name, Department, Semester, and CGPA, and serves them to clients over the network.

Two implementations are built: a TCP version (1a) where the server accepts multiple clients concurrently using threads and returns the complete academic profile for the requested Roll Number, and a UDP version (1b) where the client checks whether a Roll Number exists and receives the student's name as a datagram. In both versions the server returns "Student Record Not Found." for unknown Roll Numbers. The two implementations are then compared (1c) on connection, reliability, ordering, error recovery, and communication.

rows: Connection
Connection-oriented: three-way handshake before data transfer and explicit close
Connectionless: datagrams are sent directly with no setup or teardown
Reliability
Reliable: guaranteed delivery with acknowledgments and retransmission of lost segments
Unreliable: best-effort delivery, datagrams may be lost without detection
Ordering
Ordered: segments are sequenced and delivered in the same order they were sent
Unordered: datagrams may arrive out of order
Error Recovery
Recovers from errors: ACKs, retransmission, and flow control
No recovery: only checksum-based error detection, damaged packets are dropped
Communication
Stream-oriented with higher overhead (larger headers, connection state)
Message-oriented with lower overhead (small 8-byte header), faster and simpler

Create TCP server
Bind to 127.0.0.1:5002; spawn one thread per accepted client
Two clients connected and were served at the same time
TCP record found

TCP record not found
Client sent 9999999999; no matching record in the CSV

Create UDP server
Bind UDP socket to 127.0.0.1:5003; reply with sendto for every datagram
UDP Student Record Server Started; sender IP/port shown per request
UDP record found
Client sent 3122245001006; server confirmed the record and sent the name
Client received "Name: Divya Nair" as the datagram reply
UDP record not found
Client sent 8888888888; no matching record in the CSV
Server returned "Student Record Not Found."
Graceful termination
Client closes its connection after the reply; other clients unaffected
Server kept running and logged both disconnections cleanly

sections.heading: LEARNING OUTCOMES
bullets: I read a CSV file with csv.DictReader and built a lookup dictionary keyed by Roll Number.
I implemented a threaded TCP server that serves multiple student clients concurrently.
I implemented a connectionless UDP server and clients using sendto() and recvfrom().
I handled both found and not-found cases with the exact message "Student Record Not Found."
I compared TCP and UDP on connection, reliability, ordering, error recovery, and communication.
I observed that a print lock is needed when multiple threads log to the same console.
